The base fighter-type in The Bard's Tale, warriors can use nearly every weapon there is. For every 4 levels of experience after the 1st, Warriors get an extra attack ability in combat.

Paladins are fighters who have sworn to abstain from all evil and to uphold honor and purity in all places. They can use most weapons and some that no other fighters can. They get multiple attacks at higher levels. They also have a greatly increased resistance to evil magic.

A professional thief with so-so combat ability, the rogue can hide in shadows, and leap out at distant enemies to land critical hits. They can also search for traps and disarm them. Without a rogue your party will pay very dearly for the booty it wins.

The Bard is a wandering minstrel. You'll see them with a tankard of ale in front of them in the less reputable taverns -- the rowdier the better. Their song magic can help your party immensely in and out of combat.

An assassin, a mercenary, a ninja. The hunter can use most weapons, and has the ability (which grows with experience) to do critical hits in combat (i.e., to attack a nerve center or other vital area and instantly kill an opponent). A good skill.
A martial artist, an almost inhuman fighting machine trained to fight without weapons or armor. The monk can use them, but, at higher levels particularly, often does better without.
Conjurers deal in the physical creation and manifestation of real things (like fire, light, healing).
Magicians deal with magic as it affects physical objects (i.e., enchanting a sword, making armor stronger, making a dungeon wall disappear).
Sorcerers are magic users who deal with the creation and manipulation of illusion. Due to the power of sorcerer spells, this class is not available to newly created characters.

Wizards are magic users who are dedicated to the summoning and binding of various supernatural creatures. These creatures are not friendly to humankind and trying to control them is extremely hazardous. The Wizard-class is not available to new characters either.

These magic users have learned at least three levels for each of the previous four magic user classes. The Archmage is one of the most powerful and important characters in The Destiny Knight because an Archmage can do almost anything. Remember, Lagoth Zanta is an Archmage... fight fire with fire.

Chronomancers are the travel experts of the magic users. Before becoming one, a magic user must master all the spells of any three mage classes. And once you become a Chronomancer, you lose the power to use all the spells you previously learned. It may sound unfair, but the Chronomancer needs to focus all of his or her attention on the important dimension teleport spells. Don't think you can get around without this spellcaster, because you just can't.

Fighters who want to convert to a life of a magic can become Geomancers. Once they choose to change, they can still use the armor, weapons, and magic items that the fighter classes use. Beware: Bards lose their songs, Warriors lose their multiple attacks, Hunters lose their critical hit ability, and Monks lose their armor class bonus and multiple attacks. It's part of the trade off. To become a Geomancer, you must find the one special location that performs the rite of passage to this mage class.
While possibly being of hardier stock, this character is nonetheless like you or me.
Patterned after the Tolkien elf, the elf is slight of build, frequently taller and nimbler than a human, and very inclined to magic.
The Dwarven people are short and stout, extremely strong and healthy, but not amazingly intelligent (i.e. excellent fighters).
Hobbits are slightly smaller than Dwarves but are nimble and dexterous. Just the right make-up for a rogue.
These crossbreeds are usually blond and fair-skinned, like elves, and get some added size and strength from their human ancestry.

An orc is a large, goblin-like creature often found working for evil wizards. The Half-orc, being half human, is not quite as despicable as his orc parent, but you wouldn't want to date one. They are tough but incredibly stupid.
Gnomes closely resemble dwarves, but have less hair and even shorter tempers. They are also more magically inclined, as a rule. Highly intelligent but not very robust.
Strength is physical power and chiefly affects the amount of damage a character can do to an opponent in hand-to-hand combat. Make sure your fighting characters are strong.
Intelligence is mental power. A high intelligence will enable your magic users to get bonus spell points.
Measures agility & nimbleness. A high score makes your characters harder to hit and helps them strike the first blow in combat.
Measures healthiness. It takes more damage to kill a character with a high constitution score. This is reflected in bonus "hit points", the character's life span.
Luck is an ambiguous attribute, as it has a number of unseen effects on gameplay. For example, lucky characters are more likely to resist evil magic and avoid nasty traps.
Hit Points measure the damage a character can take before they are killed. The current status is shown in the characters status bar, followed by their current maximum potential.

My name is Saradon, a wizard of some fame and little fortune. Though you know me not, and we have never met, I feel that I have known you all my life. For the story of your deeds, your entanglement with Mangar and his evil horde in Skara Brae, flows from the lips of every Bard throughout the Realm.

For this reason, for your courage and experience, I have contacted you above all others. For now we face an evil much greater than Mangar's. An evil that threatens not the safety and tranquility of but one city, nae... an evil that threatens the existence of the entire Realm and all the cities and citizens within!

Recall now the lessons of your childhood. The story of Turin, the Archmage who forged the Destiny Wand in the molten depths of the holy mountain Krontor. The Destiny Wand, the uniting force which has rallied armies to the aid of the Realm, and has maintained peace and prosperity for the last 700 years.

But look around you now, where has the power of the Destiny Wand gone? Lawless mercenaries from the neighboring kingdom of Lestradae have invaded the Realm and now run rampant through the streets. Even in Tangramayne, our capital! It is they who have taken the Destiny Wand, with the guidance of an evil Archmage known as Lagoth Zanta.

Although Lagoth has thwarted each of my attempts to gain knowledge of his powers and location, I have been able to discover that the Destiny Wand lies broken in seven pieces, at seven different locations. Lagoth has placed each fragment of the scepter within a Snare of Death - a puzzle room that will require all the wisdom and cunning at your disposal in order for you to survive.

Do you believe in legends?\n\nLegend states that, Unimaginable power is bestowed upon the one who reforges the Destiny Wand... Regardless of whether or not you hold faith in the stuff of legend, you must defeat Lagoth Zanta, regain the seven fragments, and reforge the Destiny Wand - it is the only way to save the Realm.

Now I must hurry, for in my attempts to glean knowledge of Lagoth, he has discovered my prying magic and even now his mercenaries approach. I care not for my own safety, but I pray that my magic is still strong enough to deliver this letter into your hands.

My workshop contains powerful quest knowledge which I have gathered using magic and other, more physical, methods. Use it to help you during your quest. My only regret is that I cannot personally be there to counsel you during your quest. May fate smile upon you... and upon me.\n\nSaradon.

THE LEGEND OF SKARA BRAE



Long ago in the land of Caith, when magic still prevailed, the evil wizard Mangar the Dark threatened a small but harmonious town called Skara Brae. Overnight, all the town's militiamen disappeared, and Mangar froze the surrounding countryside with a spell of Eternal Winter, totally isolating it from any possible help. 



As evil creatures oozed into the sewers to join Mangar’s shadow crusade, the future of Skara Brae hung in the balance. And who was left to resist? Only a handful of unproven young Warriors, some junior magic users, a couple of Bards barely old enough to drink, and a few out of work Rogues.



You are the leader of this ragtag group of freedom fighters. Luckily you have a Bard with you to sing your glories - if you survive - for this is the stuff of legends. 



And thus the story begins...
"The song I sing\nwill tell the tale\nof a cold and wintery day"
"When evil fled\nand brave men bled\nthe Dark One came to stay."
"Of castle walls\nand torchlit halls\nand a price men had to pay."
"Till men of old\nfor blood and gold\nhad rescued Skara Brae."

A LETTER RECEIVED



Greetings, heroes! My name is Saradon, a wizard of some fame and little fortune. Every bard in Caith sings of your victory over Mangar and his vile horde in Skara Brae. Thus, even though we have never met, I am seeking you out.



Our land now faces a danger even greater than Mangar - an evil that could leave it open to invasion and bloody conquest. The Destiny Wand, which has kept us safe for seven hundred years, has been shattered into seven fragments by the Archmage Lagoth Zanta, and those fragments hidden all across the realm. Until you recover them, reforge the wand, and defeat Lagoth Zanta, Caith is in peril. Save her, I beg you.



Now I must hurry, for while I was attempting to glean knowledge of Zanta, he sensed my prying magic, and even now his Lestradae mercenaries approach. I care not for my own safety, but I pray my magic will keep this letter safe until it reaches your hands. May fate smile upon you... and me.

As I lay dying...



I leave this record so those who come after will know what horrors that the Mad God Tarjan has perpetrated, and so that they will not be lulled into believing that Skara Brae was his sole target.



We held a great festival to celebrate the victory over Mangar. Then Mangar's Master, The Mad God Tarjan, arrived... His shadow ravaged the city and foul creatures burst forth to assault fair Skara Brae. People ran, but Tarjan's minions left none untouched.

 Tarjan gloated that Skara Brae was merely one in a series of conquests that would complete his revenge. He laughed when I promised that the legendary Hawkslayer, and those who defeated Mangar, would return again to triumph. As payment for my threat, he gave a swift twist of his jewelled sword into my belly. 



Tarjan must be stopped, for upon this rests the fate of more than Skara Brae, more than Caith. Failure will mean the extinction of all life - save for the wretched Tarjan and his servile parasites. Pray for success... and life renewed.

Come hear the tale of Skara Brae -

A god returned to have his way.

Creatures of darkness, spawn of night,

The Mad One's kin destroyed the site.

Defenders fell, their bane come true,

Garth, Roscoe, Kylearan too!

As doom approached, the helpless fled.

It did no good, the streets ran red.

Survivors few, they sit and mope,

with but one final ray of hope:

Cross time and space, the legends say,

Heroes, at last! To steal the day!

"Welcome, brave heroes. You have succeeded in destroying

the threat to all reality. As you know, to do this, you slipped

the bonds of time, and traveled forbidden routes through that

which has forever been. You pressed your struggle forward

despite danger and death, and you accomplished that which

the gods themselves were unable to do."

His praise washes over you like a warm ocean wave, and

you feel strength infuse your body. "In doing what you have

done, you have proven yourself worthy of nothing less than

the ultimate reward." He closes his eyes and raises his hands.

"The death of the gods tore reality asunder, but you bound

as my new children. You shall be gods yourselves!"

His eyes open again and you look upon infinity. At once you see

Skara Brae restored to its former beauty. You see beyond it

and the Six cities of the Plains. You see the whole world and 

each of its cultures, and you realize all of it is now your domain.

Like a boxing match, combat is divided into a series of rounds. At the beginning of each round, a decision must be made for what action each character will perform in the upcoming fight. At the beginning of the round a menu of battle options will appear in the , displaying the actions each character can perform the following round. There are several , some are specific. Enemies appear within a range of 10' to 90' feet from the party. Melee range is 10’ feet. Enemies 10' feet away are in melee range and can attack or be attacked with hand-held weapons. can choose to hide in shadows and, if successful, can increase their range by 10’ feet each combat round until they perform an attack. Only the first 4 characters and the first 4 rows of monsters can be attacked physically, as long as they are within . The last 3 characters can only be struck by magical and ranged attacks, and can only attack back, with magic or ranged weapons. This simulates the first 4 party-members being up on the front line of attack, with the last 3 characters acting as backup in case one of the first 4 is killed. The first 4 groups of monsters are in a similar position, they are the only enemies who can attack or be attacked physically. Once all the choices for characters have been entered, the round begins. The most characters or monsters usually make the first strike, but , and also affect this. In evenly matched fights, the outcome often depends on which side gets in the first blow. At the end of a combat round, the monsters that are killed, are removed from the foe’s ranks so their bodies don’t pile up and interfere with battle. A fresh group of monsters may also advance into the first 4 ranks to assist their fellow monsters. If party member dies in combat, they are shuffled to the bottom of the party list. When all of the enemies or party members in combat are dead (whichever comes first) - combat is over. Successfully defeating enemies in combat, awards each party member (characters only) . The amount of XP awarded varies based on difficulty of the fight, the number of enemies defeated and the number of characters who survive. Surviving combat also offers the potential for the party to find a . Combat with enemies occurs both randomly and at set locations. Intra-party combat (Party Attack) can be initiated at almost any time, in case one of the members has become hostile. The rate of scrolling of the combat messages can be .

Melee combat is the act of physically assaulting enemies. Melee combat always takes place within 10' feet. Only the first 4 characters and the first 4 groups of monsters can be attacked physically. Melee damage can only be inflicted on enemies if they are in within melee range. Anything further than that, and the party members out of range will have to advance, throw a weapon or use an item to inflict damage. Weapons that have a range and the ability to be thrown, although they might not return. Weapons that can be thrown can still be used in melee combat (without throwing them). Critical Hit Critical hits are an attack that hits a nerve center or other vital area which kills an opponent instantly. and have the ability to perform critical hits. Rogues only have the ability to do so when hidden in shadows. Multiple Attacks Multiple attacks is the ability to attack the enemy with multiple hits within a single round of combat. , and have the ability to perform multiple attacks.

Ranged combat is the act of attacking enemies from a distance.

Range is represented by 10' - 90' feet. 20'+ is always ranged.



Weapons that are thrown or shot are known as missile weapons and have a range in which they are effective. To use arrows, a bow must be equipped. Missile weapons are usually nonrecoverable - they can be used only once. There are, of course, exceptions to this rule. Some magical missile weapons such as Zen arrows can be reused, and at least one non magical missile weapon, the boomerang, can be reused because it returns to the one who threw it.



<l="MAN_ITEMS","Weapons and items"/> will always display their maximum range.

The Guild is like a union hall where adventurers hang out, hoping to join a party. This is where a party is formed and where all adventures begin. A party can have a total roster of 7 characters. Characters can also be added, removed, renamed, change their portrait, or permanently delete them. Entire parties can also be saved or deleted. There is a pre-built party - The A-TEAM, ready to jump straight into gameplay. They might not have the best or but they get the job done. In Tales of the Unknown (BT1), and The Destiny Knight (BT2), the game starts in the Adventurer's Guild. In Thief of Fate (BT3), the game starts in the . The Adventurer's Guild and the refugee camp are the only spots a party can be formed, characters created, and parties saved. If an entire party roster dies while out and about, they will be transported, still dead, to the guild. By creating and adding a live character, the new very much alive character can then ferry the dead characters to a to resurrect them, or just remove or delete them and create new characters. Visiting an Adventurer's Guild makes time seem like it's flying by. When exiting, it always turns night to day. The Adventurer's Guild is always open.

Once, there was a home to travellers called the . Wayfarers stopped there when they wanted to slake a thirst, engage in merriment, or just rest their weary feet. Now that the plague has descended and Skara Brae has been shattered, the Refugee Camp serves as the gathering point for travellers. The Refugee Camp is the same as the Adventurer's Guild, although lacking the niceties like tables, heating and vermin-free bedding, they do the same things. If an entire party roster dies while out and about, they will be transported, still dead, to the camp. By creating and adding a live character, the new very much alive character can then ferry the dead characters to a to resurrect them, or just remove or delete them and create new characters. Visiting the refugee camp, it will make time seem like it's flying by. When exiting, it always turns night to day. The refugee camp is always open.

The Review Board is a group of high level representatives from all 13 different . Upon an in person request, the board will determine whether a character has accumulated enough experience points for advancement to higher . The board teaches new to magic users who qualify for higher too, but charges for this training. Review Boards are closed at night.

Garth is one of yesterday's almost forgotten heroes, now retired from active adventuring to supply tomorrow's would-be greats. At Garth's shoppe characters can buy armor and weapons, sell items, have items identified, or pool all the party's gold for buying expensive items.



Due to a deal with the city blacksmith, Garth has an infinite supply of basic armor and supplies. But unique Items found in labyrinths, even if sold to Garth, remain in his inventory only until they are sold. Occasionally an item won in combat will remain unidentified. This means that its general type might be apparent such as a shield or ring, but not which exact type, like a dragon shield or ring of power.



Garth can identify items... for a price.



Garth's shop is <u>closed</u> at night.

If spell points aren't re-charging fast enough, visit Roscoe's energy emporium. Roscoe will replenish a single or all magic users spell points for a fee. But be prepared for electrifyingly high fees. 



Roscoe can identify specials traits of weapons, armor and items... for a price.



Roscoes is <u>open</u> at night.

Taverns are favorite places to obtain refreshment and gossip. Watch in taverns - they have a tendency to over tip the bartender and - tip over the barmaid. Order a drink for a bard to refresh the amount they can sing. Taverns are open at night.

Temples are divine places of resurrection and complete healing.



A resurrected character retains all the items, gold and experience points they had before dying, but comes back to life with only 1 hit point.



When they finds out how much it cost to be resurrected, they may turn over their grave.



Temples are <u>open</u> at night.

Levels higher or lower than the parties current level, can be navigated to by using , , or - whichever is more convenient or readily available. Stairways are not visible from a distance. But when the party moves onto one, a prompt will appear in the asking whether to ascend or descend. Each succeeding level goes up in a tower, and down in a dungeon.

Portals are holes in the floors and ceilings, and are visible from a distance. The party will not go through a portal merely by standing on it. They must first be instructed to do so. The skull at the top of the , shows information related to the current effects on the party within dungeons. When the skull's eyes are not glowing, the dungeon has no aura and the party is in a harm free space. When the skull's eyes are glowing, it is in a state where it has information about something in the dungeon that is causing an effect on the party. Red - only a curse, active aura, event timer or general harm is affecting the party. Blue - only a blessing is affecting the party. Purple - a combination of blessings and curses. Curses A curse is a magical effect that is inflicted upon the party to hinder their ability to navigate. Curses can impair vision, stop bard songs and even stop the use of magic. Curses are commonly documented as locations. Blessings Blessings are a magical effect that benefit party members. Blessings are commonly documented as locations of . Active Aura An aura is an invisible magical essence that lurks within the dungeon. The aura can also be built directly into the dungeons structure. Auras can cause anti-magic, anti-apport or anti-phasedoor. Event Timers are time based events. The magic detection skull keeps track of the time left in these events. General Harm Sometimes the party gets into a bit of trouble, the magic detection skull also shows if the party is drowning or freezing.

Scry Sight (SCSI) is a helpful spell to identify which direction the party is facing. The direction is also pointed out in the journal, minimap and compass if the appropriate spells are active.
